dedupe_keys.name: south east europe electricity roadmap modelling the energy transition in the electricity sector

description: This case study models long-term pathways for the electricity sectors of South East Europe if the region follows the European Union's energy transition. It was published in 2018 in Climate Policy by László Szabó, Ágnes Kelemen, András Mezősi, Zsuzsanna Pató, Enikő Kácsor, Gustav Resch and Lukas Liebmann, with supplementary material on figshare. The motive is that the region must replace more than 30 percent of its fossil generation capacity by 2030 and more than 95 percent by 2050 given plant ages, while attracting too little investment. Interlinked electricity models assessed renewable deployment levels, the investment needed for deep decarbonisation of more than 94 percent below 1990 by 2050, and system-wide effects of high renewables on generation adequacy and security of supply. Key policy insights are to enable renewables integration, bring EU and Energy Community policy into national planning, weigh stranded costs of new fossil plants and gas networks, and expect a transitory role for gas under a persistent carbon price. Coverage is the South East Europe region. The supplementary files are downloadable from figshare under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the article itself may sit behind the publisher's paywall, and results reflect 2018 assumptions. Simulation uses are regional capacity planning and adequacy analysis under decarbonisation. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
name: South East Europe electricity roadmap - modelling the energy transition in the electricity sector
outcomes: The power sector of South East Europe can cut greenhouse gas emissions by more than 94 percent by 2050; natural gas plays only a transitory role under a persistent CO2 price, renewables integration is key, and stranded costs of new fossil and gas network investment should be weighed.
